scenes.say: You have a real edge. Bet too much, and you'll still lose. Here's the formula that says how much.
The Kelly criterion: the fraction of your money that grows it fastest in the long run.
A bet you win {p} of the time, even money. Kelly says bet {fstar}.
scenes.note: Computed: f* = p − (1 − p)/b · simulated 1,000 players, {bets} bets

scenes.say: After {bets} bets, the typical Kelly bettor has multiplied their money {med_kelly} times.
Bet double, {f2}, and the typical result is {med_2kelly} times. Basically nowhere.
Betting too big is worse than betting too small. Many pros use half Kelly, {fhalf}.
Your edge decides whether to play. Kelly decides how big.

takeaway: Your edge decides whether to play. Kelly decides how big.
